adjudicated_statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over C, let j: V -> X be an open immersion, and let Y=X\V with its reduced structure. Work with Q-coefficients. For every integer m, compact-support localization is a long exact sequence of mixed Hodge structures containing H_c^{m-1}(Y;Q) -> H_c^m(V;Q) -> H_c^m(X;Q). All weights of H_c^{m-1}(Y;Q) are at most m-1, and morphisms of mixed Hodge structures are strict for the weight filtration; hence Gr_m^W is exact and Gr_m^W H_c^m(V;Q) -> Gr_m^W H_c^m(X;Q) is injective. Define H_m^{BM}(Z;Q):=H_c^m(Z;Q)^vee, with no Tate twist, and T_m(Z):=W_{-m}H_m^{BM}(Z;Q). Then the induced restriction T_m(X) -> T_m(V) is surjective. Equivalently, classes in the kernel created by removing Y are subquotients of H_c^{m-1}(Y;Q), have weights at most m-1, and cannot occupy the weight-equals-degree corner. This statement does not identify H_c^m(V;Q) with H_c^m(X;Q) or with the cohomology of a projective bundle or other compactification, and it makes no claim for Deligne-Mumford stacks without an independently established compact-support mixed-Hodge formalism.
contradiction_resolution: The exact contested passage in ATT-0114, Lemma 1.1/CLM-0114-1, derives the injection from the compact-support localization sequence, the bound wt H_c^{m-1}(Y) <= m-1, and strictness of the weight filtration; it then dualizes using H_m^{BM}=H_c^m dual with no Tate twist. That reasoning is correct for separated finite-type C-schemes. REV-0161's strongest attack concerned a possible hidden identification of discriminant-complement cohomology with projective-bundle cohomology. The attack does not contradict the lemma: localization proves only that the kernel of H_c^m(V) -> H_c^m(X) has weights at most m-1, hence gives an injection after Gr_m^W; it gives neither an isomorphism of the full groups nor a Leray statement with nonconstant coefficients. The audit does, however, reject the originating attempt's unqualified Deligne-Mumford-stack scope. Deligne's simplicial construction supports ordinary stack cohomology but is not, by itself, a cited construction of compactly supported cohomology or Borel-Moore homology for stacks. Tubach's later six-functor theory supplies a possible modern stack-level repair, but that is additional infrastructure not established in ATT-0114. No independently retrieved primary source explicitly verified the proposed rational compact-support comparison with coarse spaces in the exact Betti mixed-Hodge conventions used there. The promoted statement is therefore narrowed to schemes; this still covers the load-bearing applications U subset A and Z^(1) subset D identified in ATT-0114 and REV-0161. Reduced structure on Y is harmless for rational Betti cohomology. With H_m^{BM}(Z;Q) defined as H_c^m(Z;Q)^vee, no Tate twist occurs; because H_c^m has weights at most m, its dual has weights at least -m, so W_{-m}H_m^{BM} is the dual of Gr_m^W H_c^m. This also fixes the direction: dualizing the corner injection gives T_m(X) -> T_m(V) surjective. The finding is distinct from FND-0164 because it uses a degree drop from m to m-1 on the fixed closed complement, not a transfer of a constant-coefficient weight bound to a nonconstant Leray coefficient object.

excluded_claims: Deligne-Mumford stacks without a separately verified compact-support mixed-Hodge formalism
an isomorphism between the full compactly supported cohomology of the open and its compactification
weight transfer through nonconstant coefficient objects in a Leray spectral sequence
scope.included_claim: corner-weight injection for an open immersion and its dual Borel-Moore surjection
